summary: Fixed the measured defect: callback_bridge.py's deliver_callback()/deliver_callback_batch() called thread/resume then unconditionally turn/start, so a callback bound to an already-active Codex thread either started a second hidden turn or (via the busy-thread path) waited/deferred without ever appending to the in-flight turn. Verified the real installed App Server v2 JSON Schema export (/tmp/geoai-codex-app-server-schema/v2, generated before this session by prior tooling) for ThreadResumeResponse/Thread/ThreadStatus/Turn/TurnStatus/TurnSteerParams/TurnSteerResponse/CodexErrorInfo -- result.thread.status is a discriminated union ({type:idle}/{type:active,activeFlags:[...]}/{type:notLoaded}/{type:systemError}), result.thread.turns is fully populated on thread/resume, Turn.status is one of completed/interrupted/failed/inProgress, TurnSteerParams requires threadId+expectedTurnId+input, TurnSteerResponse requires only turnId, and CodexErrorInfo has an activeTurnNotSteerable{turnKind: review|compact} variant returned when turn/start or turn/steer targets a non-steerable active turn. Implemented select_steer_target(resume_response) (pure, unit-tested) which returns None for idle (existing turn/start+wait-for-turn/completed path, unchanged) or the single inProgress turn's id for active-with-exactly-one-inProgress-turn (new turn/steer path), and raises the new ActiveThreadSteerDeferralError(BusyThreadError) subclass for every other shape: notLoaded/systemError/unrecognized status, zero or multiple inProgress turns. Added AppServerClient.turn_steer() (sends threadId+expectedTurnId+input+clientUserMessageId, treats a matching TurnSteerResponse.turnId as full delivery acknowledgement without waiting for turn/completed, raises AppServerError on a turnId identity mismatch (hard, non-retryable) and ActiveThreadSteerDeferralError on any turn/steer error response (stale expectedTurnId race, activeTurnNotSteerable review/compact, or any other rejection) -- bounded deferral, never a second turn/start). Both deliver_callback() and deliver_callback_batch() now route through a shared _deliver_turn() helper that calls thread_resume() once, then dispatches to turn_start() or turn_steer() based on select_steer_target() -- turn/start is never sent to an already-active thread. ActiveThreadSteerDeferralError subclasses the existing BusyThreadError so CallbackBridge._process_batch's existing except BusyThreadError branch (requeue-or-dead-letter after DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES, client never torn down) handles every new deferral case for free with zero changes to the batch/outbox/lease machinery; the branch was updated to surface the real exception message (str(exc)) as the requeue/dead-letter reason instead of a hardcoded 'thread_busy' string, for dashboard/last_error visibility distinguishing e.g. inprogress_turn_count:0 from activeTurnNotSteerable from thread_status_not_steerable:notLoaded.
not_modified: AITools/taskdb.py -- read_first only (durable outbox/batch/lease primitives called by CallbackBridge unchanged; no batching/outbox schema change was needed for this repair), not in this task's allowed_writes, not touched.

schema_verification.ThreadResumeResponse.json -> Thread: required includes status, turns (turns fully populated on thread/resume per its own description, not just thread/read)
schema_verification.CodexErrorInfo.activeTurnNotSteerable: {turnKind: NonSteerableTurnKind[review|compact]} -- documented as 'Returned when turn/start or turn/steer is submitted while the current active turn cannot accept same-turn steering, for example /review or manual /compact'
schema_verification.conclusion: Confirms the implementation's exact routing decision (idle->turn/start, active-with-one-inProgress-turn->turn/steer, everything else->bounded deferral) and the activeTurnNotSteerable error shape used by _fake_app_server.py's --active-not-steerable scenario and AppServerClient.turn_steer()'s error handling.

real_bug_fixed.bug: deliver_callback()/deliver_callback_batch() called self.thread_resume(thread_id) purely for its identity-check side effect and then unconditionally called self.turn_start(...) regardless of the resumed thread's actual status -- an already-active thread (one still running a long CEO review turn) would either receive a second concurrent turn/start (if the real App Server permits queueing rather than erroring) or hit the pre-existing generic busy-error path with no way to ever append feedback into the in-flight turn; the callback would sit as a dead letter/timeout instead of being delivered.
real_bug_fixed.fix: select_steer_target() inspects result.thread.status/result.thread.turns from the SAME thread/resume response already being made and returns either None (idle -> unchanged turn/start path) or the exact single inProgress turn id (active -> new turn/steer path) or raises a bounded ActiveThreadSteerDeferralError for every ambiguous/non-steerable shape -- turn/start is now structurally never reachable when the thread is already active.
real_bug_fixed.status: FIXED -- proven by test_active_thread_steers_existing_turn_without_turn_start_or_wait (turn/steer succeeds, no turn/completed ever sent by the fake server, no hang) and test_turn_start_is_forbidden_and_rejected_on_an_active_thread (defense-in-depth: the fake server itself rejects any turn/start reaching it while active, catching a future regression loudly).

blockers: The production VS Code OpenAI extension owns a long-lived App Server over private stdio. A separately spawned bridge App Server does not share its in-memory active-turn state, reports the visible owner thread idle, and therefore cannot safely steer the current UI turn.
